answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post offers, then slash that stake when independently verified trades reveal fraud. A single operator can still create many identities, but each one ties up capital and risks forfeiture; splitting activity across accounts does not erase that cost. A ripple of linked trades can expose a coordinated cluster, while an onyx account or a meadow of new profiles gains no trust merely from looking distinct.
